messages:
alex: seeing a ton of pod connection drops in eu-west3 GPU pool, started ~10:04 UTC, service impacts for model infer pods :grimacing:
ritika: any kernel logs? last time we had nf_conntrack messages when the pool flapped
alex: dmesg shows `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet` and a bunch of `nf_conntrack: timeout` churn
carla: ugh, that usually means ephemeral port churn + many short-lived connections. did something restart sidecars?
alex: yes — we had a noisy rollout of the model-sidecar (hash ring) across nodes, lots of 503 retries and reconnect storms
mike: spike looks correlated with sidecar restarts. conntrack count per node: `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` was ~250k on the worst nodes
ritika: what's nf_conntrack_max right now?
alex: `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` -> 262144 (set during node bootstrap)
sre-bot: deploy: rollout finished for model-sidecar v1.12 at 10:02 UTC (no errors reported)
carla: 262k isn't terrible but with many short connections + NAT port reuse, you can hit table full quickly. Also saw `nf_conntrack: table full` in kube-proxy logs on some nodes
mike: quick mitigation: increase nf_conntrack_max and reduce timeouts for TCP_ESTABLISHED/TCP_CLOSE where safe. Also drop conntrack for CLOSED states quicker.
ritika: agreed. proposed commands (one-off):
```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=120
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_close=10
```
carla: also tune hashsize if we change max: `echo $((524288/4)) > /sys/module/nf_conntrack/parameters/hashsize` (careful, requires module reload on some kernels)
alex: rolling that now to the 6 most impacted GPU nodes. doing a restart of kube-proxy after sysctl to ensure iptables rules re-evaluate
mike: longer-term: we should make sidecar backoffs more aggressive and/or add connection pooling so we don't open 100s of ephemeral connections per request for warmup traffic
alex: agreed. I'll patch sidecar to reuse HTTP/1.1 keepalive for prefetch paths and add a jittered retry window to avoid thundering herd
ritika: another thing: check CNI NAT masquerade config — if we can enable `hairpin` or `local-allow` for these nodes it reduces SNAT churn (fewer ephemeral ports consumed)
carla: for RDMA-enabled nodes we saw similar symptoms but different root cause — MTU mismatch + TCP retransmits increase conntrack lifetimes. worth verifying `ip link` MTU on GPU nodes
mike: good call. run `ip -o link show dev <iface>` and `ss -tan sport = :<port>` to verify flows and retransmits
alex: mitigation applied to 6 nodes. conntrack count dropped to ~80k, no new drops seen in last 2m :thumbsup:
sre-bot: incident-note: marking incident open -> mitigation in progress. notify #oncall if regressions
ritika: follow-ups: (1) create a kube-daemonset to set sysctl across nodes persistently and expose as node config (2) add a Prom alert for conntrack usage > 70% per-node (3) schedule sidecar backoff patch PR
mike: I'll own the alert and the DS. alex please add the runtime sysctl changes to the node bootstrap template after we validate no regressions
alex: will do. also adding a short-runbook snippet about this cause (sidecar restart storm -> conntrack exhaustion) to incidents repo
carla: thanks team. removing noisy rollout from the model-sidecar canary until we have the backoff fix
alex: noted, pausing canary and reverting the rollout in the k8s control plane now
ritika: closing loop: will re-evaluate after 24h and decide on permanent nf_conntrack_max bump vs app fix. prefer app fix + alerting first
carla: 👍
